title: Pager signal sculpting and automated fallthrough handler
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce noisy pages and improve on-call actionability by aligning alerting thresholds to SLO violations, introducing a fast fallthrough handler that can apply circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies automatically, and producing concise runbooks with automated remediation steps. Scope: alerts from serving runtime (request queue latency, token generation tail latency, batching overruns), regional failover signals, and SLO breach indicators. Out of scope for this ticket: billing alerts and infra-level hardware faults (handled by infra ops).
acceptance_criteria: Reduce noise (page volume) for the targeted alerts by >=50% during steady-state synthetic traffic in canary region without increasing time-to-detect for real incidents
Implement an automated fallthrough handler that can apply a circuit-breaker for a noisy route and trigger staged load-shedding policies (graceful degradation) for affected regions
Ship a short on-call runbook template (2 screens) with clear escalation, rollback, and telemetry queries for triage that auto-populates with runbook context from the handler
Add tracing and dashboard widgets to show when fallthrough handlers activate and their decision rationale (reason code, metrics snapshot)
Integration tests and a simulated incident run show no customer-facing errors during a controlled failover exercise
checklist: Design: define signal taxonomy (noise vs. incident) and SLO-aligned thresholds - DONE
Design: fallthrough handler decision model and policy table (circuit-breaker, per-route shedding levels) - DONE
Implementation: handler service skeleton and policy store - IN PROGRESS

comments: 2026-03-05 Asha Patel: Created ticket. Initial spike indicates a large fraction of pages are caused by transient KV cache misses that self-heal within 30s. Need a short suppression window tied to cache-miss rate and SLO impact.

2026-03-06 Liam Chen: Ran correlation between pages and region-scale autoscale events. Found 2 spikes linked to batched request queue overflow during pod churn. Suggest adding a pre-filter that looks at queue-depth + pod-state to mute pages until state stabilizes.

2026-03-08 Design review (Riley Martinez): Reviewed fallthrough policy table. Proposed policy priority: 1) suppress if transient signal with <3s half-life, 2) circuit-breaker open if error rate > 2% sustained for 60s and routing fallback exists, 3) progressive load-shedding (10/30/50%) when latency percentile exceeds SLO and fallback fails.

2026-03-09 Implementation note (Liam Chen): Pushed handler skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reliability/compare/eng-752990. Uses policy-store v2 and emits an event via /telemetry/fallthrough. PR #4821 opened for review.

2026-03-10 QA (Maya Singh): Added synthetic test harness that replays the last major incident trace and injects cache misses. Early results: suppression reduced pages by 68% but detection time for true degradation increased by ~8s for one alert type. Need to tighten detection path for SLO-breach alerts.

2026-03-12 Product (Evan Zhao): Confirmed customer_impact medium and requested a short runbook UI template that highlights affected model routes and quick rollback to previous routing policy. Also requested a postmortem hook that records the handler decision for audit.
2026-03-12 Security (Priya Kapoor): Reviewed policy-store access. No secrets needed but require RBAC for policy edits. Filing ENG-753012 to add RBAC checks in policy admin UI.
implementation_notes: Handler emits structured event with keys: reason_code, metric_snapshot (text summary), affected_routes, action_taken. Integrate with console to show these as timeline entries on the incident page. Circuit-breaker states will be persisted for 5 minutes by default with exponential backoff. Policy store entries are versioned; rollbacks possible via Console UI.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression could delay detection of slow-onset incidents. Mitigation: SLO-aligned carveouts — alerts tied to SLO breach metrics bypass short suppression windows.
Risk: Mis-configured shedding policy could harm customer requests. Mitigation: Canary rollout and gradual escalation (10% -> 30% -> 50%) with automatic rollback if error rate increases.
Risk: RBAC gaps on policy edits. Mitigation: ENG-753012 to add policy-admin RBAC and audit logs before GA.
Risk: Increased complexity for on-call. Mitigation: concise runbook cards and a one-click revert in Console.
